newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ committee reopens debate on NZ$94 mln building.
newsitem.headline: NZ committee reopens debate on NZ$94 mln building.

text.p: Parliament's Government Administration select committee on Thursday reopened the debate over the planned NZ$94 million Cabinet building.
Committee chairman Clem Simich told Reuters the committee had agreed to call for public submissions after receiving a petition from voters. It would report to parliament before the end of June.
The government in April approved the building, dubbed "the parliamentary palace" by its critics, after reconsidering the plan in the face of strong public opposition.
This week a 200,000 signature petition opposing the building was presented to parliament.
Committee member and free-market Act Party MP Rodney Hide, who campaigned against the building, said the petition had forced a rethink.
"It is clear to me that if the Palace was put to a free vote in the House, it would be voted down," Hide said.
Finance ministers and some government backbenchers had expressed concern about the expenditure and the process of selecting the final building design.
